data.name: Sankara
data.gender_notes: Sankara is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who brings peace and harmony, derived from the God Shiva. The name Sankara carries the meaning “Conducive to Peace” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Sankara usually hope their child will grow to embody conducive to peace and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the supreme consciousness and the ultimate reality
data.etymology: Sankara belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Conducive to Peace.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sankara total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_sanskrit.name: संकर
in_sanskrit.meaning: One who brings about change or transformation
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The one who is the embodiment of all the divine qualities and knowledge, and is responsible for the transformation of the universe towards its ultimate goal of spiritual enlightenment. This name is derived from the Sanskrit root 'san' which means 'to put together' and 'kar' which means 'action'. Thus, Sankara means 'one who brings about change or transformation'.

in_hindi.name: संकर
in_hindi.long_meaning: The one who brings happiness and contentment to others. This name is derived from the Hindi words 'san' which means 'complete' and 'kar' which means 'do'. Thus, Sankara means 'one who brings happiness and contentment to others'.

in_tamil.name: ஸங்கர
in_tamil.long_meaning: The one who brings together or unites. This name is derived from the Tamil word 'sankar' which is derived from the Sanskrit root 'san' which means 'to put together'. Thus, Sankara means 'one who brings together or unites'.

in_telugu.name: సంకర
in_telugu.long_meaning: The one who is complete in all respects. This name is derived from the Telugu word 'sankar' which is derived from the Sanskrit root 'san' which means 'complete'. Thus, Sankara means 'one who is complete in all respects'.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sankara holds deep cultural significance in Hinduism, as it is derived from the revered deity, Lord Shiva, who is known as the God of destruction and later, regeneration. The name evokes feelings of peace, harmony, and a sense of bringing about positive change. It also highlights the cyclical nature of life and the inherent balance and order that underpins the universe.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, the name Sankara is believed to imbue its bearer with the qualities of Shiva – renunciation, detachment, and ultimate spiritual wisdom. It is a reminder of the eternal truth that lies beneath the transient material world. The name is a source of inspiration and strength, reminding its bearer to be compassionate, peaceful, and ever mindful of the divine within oneself and all beings.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sankara symbolizes the purifying force of Shiva, seeking to remove ignorance and lead the soul towards ultimate enlightenment. It represents the convergence of all opposites, uniting dualities and leading to the realization of the non-dual, divine consciousness.
